mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified corporate registry extract confirming registration of Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office at the competent district court of the corporate domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive paths: (i) Apostille member recipient state: obtain certified Korean registry extract, then request Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; no consular legalization. (ii) Non-member recipient state: obtain certified Korean registry extract, then Korean MOFA authentication, then legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate of the recipient state; do not chain or combine the two paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing equivalent (valid Korean business registration certificate and tax clearance certificate showing no delinquency)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the competent local tax office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive paths: (i) Apostille member recipient state: obtain notarized certified copies from NTS or its authorized platform, then MOFA Apostille; no consular legalization. (ii) Non-member recipient state: obtain notarized certified copies, then MOFA authentication, then consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate of the recipient state; never combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation, UBO filing, bank account opening, and execution of aviation escrow and SWIFT wire instructions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial shareholders and first board of directors of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive paths: (i) Apostille member recipient state: notarize resolution and POA, then MOFA Apostille; no consular legalization. (ii) Non-member recipient state: notarize, then MOFA authentication, then legalization by Korean embassy or consulate of recipient state; the two authentication mechanisms are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeong-gwan) of the Chusik Hoesa, including object clause for distribution of surplus commercial aircraft parts and avionics
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and a Korean notary public, with the authenticated original maintained at the registry office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive paths: (i) Apostille member recipient state: obtain notarized certified copy of the registered Articles, then MOFA Apostille; no consular legalization. (ii) Non-member recipient state: obtain notarized certified copy, then MOFA authentication, then consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate of the recipient state; never apply both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Institutional Bank Reference Letter from a licensed Korean commercial bank confirming account behavior, transaction facilities, and escrow readiness for aviation payments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank (e.g., Citibank Korea, Kookmin Bank, or similar) where the corporate foreign currency and escrow accounts are established
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive paths: (i) Apostille member recipient state: bank letter notarized by a Korean notary, then MOFA Apostille; no consular legalization. (ii) Non-member recipient state: bank letter notarized, then MOFA authentication, then legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate of the recipient state; Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and may not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Investment Report Certificate and related proof of inward remittance (if a foreign shareholder is registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korea Trade and Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive paths: (i) Apostille member recipient state: obtain certified copy, then MOFA Apostille; no consular legalization. (ii) Non-member recipient state: obtain certified copy, then MOFA authentication, then consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate of the recipient state; the paths are never combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening must be performed before incorporation and continuously thereafter against the U.S. OFAC SDN List and 50% Rule, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury sanctions, Korean FIU/KFSC administrative sanctions list, Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance designation list, and any domestic aviation trade denial lists. Politically Exposed Persons include senior executives, judicial and legislative officers, military commanders, state-owned enterprise leaders, and international organization principals; family members and close associates must be identified. Enhanced due diligence requires source of wealth, source of funds, corporate ownership chart, independent verification of UBOs, senior management approval, adverse media review, and six-month periodic re-screening. All screening must include surname-only matching, phonetic transliteration matching, and threshold-based transaction monitoring for SWIFT wire and aviation escrow rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (e-REG / I-REG) Company Name Search and Reservation Service at iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the corporate trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be registered in Hangul; an English trade name may be used for international transactions only as a secondary registered name, and any foreign name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul. The accepted four-tier naming convention is: (1) an objective or industry descriptor such as surplus commercial aircraft parts distribution; (2) a proprietary/unique element; (3) an optional geographic or English-language placeholder; and (4) the mandatory corporate form designator Chusik Hoesa. The object clause must expressly state the distribution and wholesale trading of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus parts in Hangul to permit registration and later customs/licensing approvals.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant should first obtain the written rejection certificate and the registry name-search report identifying the conflicting trade name. The applicant may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act with the district court having jurisdiction over the rejecting registry within two weeks of receipt of the rejection. The appeal petition must annex the rejection certificate, name-search result, proposed amended Hangul and English names, UBO identity particulars, and a legal memorandum distinguishing the applicant from the conflicting entity. While the appeal is pending, the applicant may simultaneously reserve an alternative permissible name to avoid delaying incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or PO Box will not satisfy the commercial substance requirements for a licensed distributor of certified surplus commercial aircraft parts in South Korea. The National Tax Service, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and licensed banks will reject a virtual-only address for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier because the business requires import/export licensing, VAT invoice registration, physical traceability records for aircraft rotables, and personnel who can verify escrow and SWIFT wire transactions. A serviced office with a dedicated executive lease, physical reception staff, meeting room, and document storage may be acceptable if the corporation genuinely operates from that address and the address is registered with the local tax office and banking institution.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 35-45% likelihood of an unannounced National Tax Service or registry office physical inspection within the first 24 months after incorporation. Checklist for inspection: (1) original lease agreement and utility bills matching the registered office; (2) physical presence of officers, staff, or authorized agents during business hours; (3) ERP inventory system and traceability documentation for commercial aircraft parts; (4) import/export declarations and customs clearance records; (5) bank transaction and invoice records matching escrow instructions and SWIFT wires; (6) statutory distribution license or trade registration from MOLIT/MOTIE and KOTRA. Failure on any item may cause the tax authority to deny the place of effective management, reclassify corporate income, and impose penalty surcharges.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), principally Articles 289, 290, 291, 295, 296, 300, 305, 310, 312, 316, 317, 329, 331, 383, 390 and 391; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 14135, as amended), Articles 2, 4, 5 and 6; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Article 3; and the Framework Act on National Taxes and Value-Added Tax Act for subsequent tax registrations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office (Deung-gi-so) under the Supreme Court of Korea; territorial district court registry office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, including the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office for the registered address
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan); Incorporation Registration Application (Sing-sa-deung-gi) submitted to the district court; the resulting Corporate Registration Certificate (Beop-in-deung-gi-deung-bon) and Business Registration Certificate (Sa-eop-ja-deung-rok-jeung) issued by the National Tax Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The initial capital must be fully subscribed and paid into a domestic pre-incorporation subscription account before the court registration is filed, and the bank deposit certificate must be presented to the registry. For a foreign-invested entity seeking foreign-investment tax incentives, the individual case investment normally must be at least KRW 100,000,000; this is not a blocked escrow requirement but a bank-held subscription deposit that cannot be withdrawn until incorporation registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA. WHEREAS the Company is being incorporated as a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and the founding shareholders and initial directors have determined to adopt a complete corporate governance and authorization package; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AS FOLLOWS. 1. Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the issuance and subscription of the total initial authorized capital of KRW [__] comprising [__] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW [__] per share is hereby ratified and confirmed. The board acknowledges that each subscription payment, including any issue premium, has been or will be deposited before the corporate registration application into the pre-incorporation share subscription account at [bank name] under Article 295 of the Commercial Act, and that the bank deposit certificate, share subscription application, and share allocation report are adopted. The Representative Director is instructed to execute all escrow and account control agreements required by the Korean Financial Services Commission and the bank, and to ensure that no share subscription funds are withdrawn prior to registration. 2. Banking Resolutions. RESOLVED, that the opening of corporate checking, savings, foreign currency, Swift wire, and aviation settlement escrow accounts at [bank name] is approved; the Representative Director, together with any other director designated by the Representative Director, is authorized to execute all account mandates, wire instructions, signature cards and bank forms; and the board designates the corporate seal and any electronic acceptance system as binding on the Company. 3. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company is adopted at [full address], Republic of Korea, from which statutory books and audit records will be maintained; the Representative Director may execute, on behalf of the Company, the lease agreement and any relocation after board resolution and court registration. 4. Officers and Audit. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officeholders are appointed: (i) Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer [name], with full power to manage ordinary business, hire employees, execute trade contracts, and appear before courts and administrative agencies; (ii) Director [name]; (iii) the auditor or statutory inspector [name], as required under the Commercial Act for a Chusik Hoesa of this size; and (iv) the corporate secretary and AML compliance officer [name]. Each appointee accepts office and shall sign all consent and registration documents. 5. Operational Authorizations. RESOLVED, that management is authorized to apply for all business registrations, import and export declarations, aviation parts supplier registrations, environmental or fire permits, and bank onboarding approvals; procure insurance and fidelity coverage; open payroll and tax withholding accounts with the National Tax Service; and file all incorporation, foreign investment and licensing returns. Any two directors or the Representative Director alone may act for the Company where the registered corporate seal is affixed. 6. Effective Date. RESOLVED, that this Resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts, with the minutes maintained in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea i-ONE Court Portal (https://www.i-one.go.kr) and a notary public qualified under the Korean Notary Public Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Supreme Court corporate name registry to confirm that the proposed Korean company name with the suffix Chusik Hoesa is not identical to an existing registered legal entity and that no conflicting trade name registration blocks the intended name. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, setting out the corporate name, object clause limited to distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, principal office address, total authorized share capital, par value, share classes, directors terms, auditor appointment, fiscal year, and notice provisions. Submit the signed articles and each incorporator certified passport or corporate certificate to a Korean notary public. Foreign incorporators must execute a power of attorney, and any foreign corporate resolution, certificate of incorporation, or good standing certificate must be apostilled or consularized as required. The notary verifies identities, witnesses signatures, and stamps the articles before the file is scanned for court registration.
required_dossiers: executed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
certified passport copies of individual incorporators
foreign corporate charter and good standing certificate of corporate shareholders
power of attorney for the local incorporation agent
residential address and seal certificate of the representative director
completed i-ONE corporate name search report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court registry or notary queries the name, business purpose, or corporate governance clauses, amend the articles and resubmit within the statutory two-week supplementation period. Minor modifications, such as correction of the office address or share par value, may be initialed by all incorporators and require no full re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Subscription Account Opening and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank registered with the Financial Services Commission in the Republic of Korea, together with KOTRA Invest Korea for foreign investment reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-incorporation subscription account under the proposed Korean corporate name at a banking office in the Republic of Korea. Each founding shareholder must remit or transfer the full subscription price for the allocated shares, including any issue premium, before the court registration is filed. Non-resident shareholders must transmit funds through a licensed foreign exchange bank and state the remittance purpose as securities acquisition. The bank will issue a deposit certificate confirming that the funds are held for incorporation and may not be withdrawn until the company is registered. Foreign investors must file the foreign investment report with KOTRA Invest Korea or the receiving bank before or at the time of the share payment, in accordance with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and obtain a foreign investment report certificate. If the business will operate an aviation settlement escrow account, the company should arrange the corresponding post-incorporation foreign currency and escrow account documents at the same bank in order to expedite the bank client onboarding review.
required_dossiers: executed Articles of Incorporation
foreign investment report application
remittance or wire transfer record
bank-issued pre-incorporation subscription account application
passport or corporate certificate of each shareholder
share subscription applications and capital allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays the account opening due to anti-money-laundering or sanctions screening, supply the requested source-of-funds documentation such as audited financial statements, contractual sale agreements, and proof of lawful origin. If KOTRA or the receiving bank issues a supplementary request, respond within the prescribed period to prevent lapse of the foreign investment report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Incorporation Registration and Tax Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial District Court Registry Office through the i-ONE Court Portal, followed by the local National Tax Service business registration window or Hometax portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the district court registry having jurisdiction over the registered office. Submit the notarized articles of incorporation, bank deposit certificate, report on share subscription, directors and auditor certificates of acceptance, statement of the corporate seal, and foreign investment report certificate. Pay the registration tax, local education surtax, and court registry filing fee. Upon acceptance, the registry assigns the corporation registration number and issues the corporate registration certificate and certified corporate seal. After the court registration, file the business registration application with the National Tax Service within the statutory deadline. The business registration certificate is required to open operating bank accounts, issue VAT tax invoices, and import or export aircraft parts. Report all officers and the corporate seal to the local tax office through the Hometax system.
required_dossiers: incorporation registration application form
notarized Articles of Incorporation
bank deposit certificate under Article 295 of the Commercial Act
share subscription report and share allocation report
director and auditor acceptance letters
specimen corporate seal impression certificate
lease agreement or landlord consent for the registered office
foreign investment report certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementation order, provide the missing documents within 14 days. If the application is rejected, file a request for re-examination or appeal to the panel of three judges. If the business registration deadline is missed, file immediately with a written explanation and pay any applicable late-filing surcharge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Regulatory Licensing, Foreign Trade Compliance, and Physical Site Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) and Korea Office of Civil Aviation; Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy for strategic goods; local municipal fire and environmental departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete all operational prerequisites after the corporate registration certificate is issued. File the import and export business declaration in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system and obtain the customs trading compliance code before moving any aviation inventory across borders. Register as an aircraft parts supplier or distributor with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or the delegated Korea Office of Civil Aviation because the business scope includes certified surplus rotables and avionics. If any avionics or aircraft technology is listed as a strategic item or dual-use good, obtain the strategic goods export or import approval from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy. For the physical office or any warehouse staging area, obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the local fire department, and if storage area construction triggers the small-scale environmental assessment threshold, file the relevant small-scale environmental impact assessment with the municipal environmental department. Complete the bank anti-money-laundering onboarding for the aviation settlement escrow account, sign the SWIFT wire mandates, register for e-tax invoices in Hometax, and maintain an aviation parts traceability ledger for compliance audits.
required_dossiers: corporate registration certificate and business registration certificate
Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS company profile and trade code application
MOLIT and Korea Office of Civil Aviation supplier registration application
HS classification and airworthiness certificate data for covered aircraft parts
warehouse lease and floor plan with fire safety inspection documents
foreign investment report certificate
bank account resolutions and AML identification pack
list of officers, share register, and board minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOLIT, Korea Customs Service, or the municipal fire department issues a supplement or designation notice, respond within the stated statutory period and provide the corrected airworthiness, customs, or fire safety documentation. A refusal of a strategic goods license may be appealed to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and the company must not ship controlled parts until the license is endorsed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) through the Korea Office of Civil Aviation; Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS single window; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy for strategic goods; and the local fire department under the National Fire Agency
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registered Aircraft Parts Supplier and Distributor License under the Aviation Safety Act; Import Export Business Declaration and Customs Trading Code under the Foreign Trade Act; Strategic Goods Export or Import Authorization for dual-use avionics; Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire Services Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the local city or county environmental department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable for a pure office-based aircraft parts trading brokerage. If the company operates a physical warehouse or logistics staging center with a floor area exceeding 500 square meters or located in an environmentally sensitive zone, a Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment may be required under the Environmental Assessment Act instead of a full Environmental Impact Assessment. No full EIA is triggered by re-selling commercial aircraft rotables unless the operator constructs an industrial facility, coating shop, or hazardous waste treatment unit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: No process wastewater is generated by trading; domestic sanitary sewage must be connected to a public sewer meeting the Sewerage Act discharge standards. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs): No degreasing, painting, or coating operations are approved; if solvent-based cleaning is introduced, the facility must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act VOC reporting and emission thresholds, including registration when annual solvent consumption reaches the regulated quantity. Hazardous waste: Rejected lithium batteries, hydraulic fluid containers, mercury-containing avionics, and chemically treated composites must be segregated, labeled, and transported by a licensed hazardous waste collector under the Wastes Control Act, with manifests retained for the five-year statutory compliance period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate and fire systems inspection approval from the local fire station for any office, warehouse, or mixed-use aviation spares storage area, including installation of automatic fire detection, extinguishing systems, and emergency egress compliant with the Fire Services Act. For racked storage of aircraft rotables or engine components, submit structural load certification and rack stability inspections. Electrical installations must receive Korea Electrical Safety Corporation inspection and certification. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, register with the Ministry of Employment and Labor when the company has five or more workers, provide workplace safety training, obtain forklift operator licenses if material handling equipment is used, and store any dangerous goods only in accordance with the Dangerous Substances and Workplace Safety regulations. A civil defense shelter obligation, if any, attaches to the building owner under the Civil Defense Act and must be noted in the lease, but no additional company-level civil defense permit is required for a distribution-only business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal at https://www.hometax.go.kr; export clearance coordination also involves the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity deriving Korean-source business income must appoint a domestic tax representative unless it has a fixed place of business in Korea. The foreign entity must submit an Application for Business Registration to the district tax office with jurisdiction over the domestic place of business, using the HomeTax portal. The application must be accompanied by certified copies of the foreign entity's charter or articles of incorporation, evidence of foreign business registration, a board resolution appointing the domestic tax representative, a signed power of attorney, and proof of the Korean business address. The National Tax Service then issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as both the Tax Identification Number and the VAT registration number. A non-resident supplier of electronic services without a domestic establishment may apply for simplified VAT registration through the HomeTax portal under the Value-Added Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not offer a check-the-box classification election. A Chusik Hoesa incorporated in Korea is subject to entity-level corporate taxation under the Corporate Tax Act. A foreign-incorporated entity whose place of effective management is in Korea may be treated as a domestic corporation, otherwise it is classified as a foreign corporation. Anti-hybrid and treaty tie-breaker rules under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act govern mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based registration threshold exists under the Value-Added Tax Act for business operators in Korea; VAT registration is mandatory from the commencement of taxable business activity. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Korean consumers are required to complete simplified VAT registration irrespective of turnover, subject to any applicable treaty relief.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoices for all VAT-registered persons. Electronic tax invoices must be issued through the HomeTax portal or an NTS-approved electronic invoicing service provider and transmitted to the National Tax Service by the end of the day following issuance. NTS receives invoice data in real time via HomeTax API and machine-to-machine filing channels. There is no separate anti-fraud digital stamping regime, but NTS operates automated cross-matching of purchase and sales invoices, customs declarations, and VAT returns; late or missing transmission attracts fixed-penalty surtaxes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply qualifies for the 0% VAT rate as an export of goods if the certified surplus commercial aircraft parts are sold to a foreign non-resident purchaser and are physically transported out of Korea within the statutory export period. The supplier must maintain evidence that legal title and risk passed to the overseas customer, that the goods were cleared by Korea Customs Service, and that export proceeds are repatriated into Korea in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Qualifying offshore services supplied to non-residents may also be zero-rated where the statutory conditions are met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic export declaration with Korea Customs export clearance record
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing Korean origin and foreign destination
Commercial invoice describing the parts as certified surplus civil aviation rotables and avionics
Packing list and export shipment evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign exchange remittance certificate) issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank
Aircraft parts airworthiness release certificate (e.g., EASA Form 1 or FAA Authorized Release Certificate 8130-3)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service will cross-check zero-rated export claims against customs clearance records, bills of lading, airworthiness documentation, and bank remittance records. If the goods are not physically exported, export documentation is falsified, or foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline, the 0% rate is reversed and 10% VAT is assessed with interest. Additional tax penalty surcharges may be imposed for negligent or intentional underreporting, totaling up to 40% or more in fraudulent cases, and criminal liability may arise. Retrospective clawback assessments are generally available for five years, extended in cases involving fraud and tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank and monetary authority, with foreign exchange policy and administration shared with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), the Financial Services Commission (FSC), and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won maintains current-account convertibility under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; ordinary export/import settlements, service fees, and profit remittances may be freely executed through licensed foreign exchange banks once supporting trade or transaction documents are presented. The capital account is partially liberalized and subject to a notification/report-and-return system rather than to simple administrative approval. Inbound foreign direct investment must be announced to a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and the contributed capital should be routed through a dedicated foreign-currency account. Profits, dividends, and liquidation proceeds from a foreign-invested entity can be remitted offshore after income tax settlement and external audit confirmation, but the legitimacy of source funds and compliance with reporting obligations must be established. The won is not freely convertible outside Korea's regulated onshore channels; offshore won trading is limited and official settlement currencies are typically USD, EUR, JPY, or CNH. A practical bottleneck is the collection of all export proceeds within statutory deadlines and the strict distinction between trade-related current account payments and capital account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Korean Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations require export proceeds to be received in Korea within 15 months from the date of export declaration. There is no fixed statutory surrender percentage requiring conversion to KRW; the full 100% of proceeds must be repatriated through a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank unless an extension or exceptional overseas-retention approval is obtained. The exporter may keep the foreign currency in a foreign currency settlement account or convert it to KRW at market rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Korean Won Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account
Korean Won Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account
Korean Won Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account
Korean Won Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs have low viability for servicing this Korean Chusik Hoesa. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, a non-bank EMI may not independently provide Korean won settlement accounts or foreign currency accounts without a domestic electronic financial business license, and under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, foreign-currency conversion and cross-border trade settlement must be channeled through licensed Korean foreign exchange banks. Therefore, offshore digital EMI rails can only be used peripherally, if at all, and cannot act as the primary treasury or trade-settlement infrastructure for inbound FDI capital or aircraft-parts disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch onboarding with at least one statutory director or the locally registered foreign-invested company representative is standard and practically mandatory for a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa under the Real-Name Financial Transaction Act and bank AML policy. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted as a sole method; the beneficial owner must still undergo an in-person identity verification or, in very limited cases, a bank-approved video interview. Apostilled corporate documents, passport, and local business registration certificate must be produced at the branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified or layer-cased beneficial ownership chain above the Chusik Hoesa, particularly foreign corporate shareholders with opaque trusts or nominee arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chart in English; certified registry extracts of all shareholders and intermediate holdings; audited financial statements; share register; proof of address; passport copies of every natural-person UBO holding 25% or more; tax residence certificates; signed UBO declaration; and bank reference letters from reputable originating banks covering the entire funding chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Surplus civil aircraft and avionics inventory is a medium-risk trade sector because of possible dual-use relevance, airworthiness fraud, or illegitimate military diversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Categorized inventory list with ISIC HS codes; original OEM or surplus purchase invoices; EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3 airworthiness release certificates; FAA/EASA traceability certificates; end-user certificates for downstream buyers; K-BEARS strategic-item transparency summary showing no export license is required or, if required, the valid license; and customs import/export records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-finance mismatch screening flags excessive invoicing, back-to-back trading, or payments routed through third parties not named in the sales contract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts; invoice; packing list; transport documents such as bill of lading or air waybill; cargo insurance policy; logistics tracking reports; customs export declarations; confirmed SWIFT MT103 covering the same route and customer; and the bank's trade-order management printout showing the underlying aircraft-part purchase order.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI equity injection lacks verifiable source of funds or is deposited from a low-disclosure jurisdiction or non-bank funding vehicle, triggering suspicion of laundering into a shell operating business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Notification certificate or bank acknowledgment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; capital remittance instruction matching the notification; 12 to 24 months of source-company bank statements; investor audited financial statements; corporate tax and VAT filings; ownership-to-funding source reconciliation; independent accountant's letter confirming no third-party lender or disguised financing; and no-cash/no-crypto source-of-wealth declaration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign parent must file the Foreign Investment Notification with KOTRA or the designated domestic foreign exchange bank before transferring capital. The equity injection is then remitted by SWIFT MT103 in USD or other eligible currency into a temporary capital-contribution foreign-currency account at a Tier 1 Korean bank. The receiving bank verifies the remitter, the parent and approval reference, and the amount against the filed investment notification; upon matching, the bank issues a capital verification report or proceed-of-investment notification enabling the Korean entity to convert the contribution to KRW and book share capital. The FX purpose code should identify foreign direct investment in equity, and the remittance reference must include the company name, entity registration ID, and foreign investment application number. No mixing with trade settlement is permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to overseas aircraft-parts suppliers, the company will use SWIFT MT103 through its Korean relationship bank for direct wire settlements, or issue or confirm commercial letters of credit in accordance with UCP600 where a supplier requires a bank payment undertaking. Documentary collections in the form of D/P or D/A are acceptable for lower-risk recurring transactional flows. USD disbursements may be made from the company's foreign-currency account or by purchasing USD from the domestic bank against the underlying import contract and customs declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to a genuine open foreign-currency trade receivable or payable and with no speculative position.
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps with a Tier 1 Korean bank to manage long-term USD-denominated working-capital or trade-finance exposure, with maturity matched to the underlying indebtedness.

Physical vanilla FX options such as purchased puts and calls or zero-cost collars concluded solely to hedge forecasted aviation-part trade settlements and reported through the bank's FX transaction reporting framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return including audited or reviewed financial statements and tax adjustment schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 for a calendar fiscal year; monthly anniversary rule for alternating fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10 percent additional tax on unpaid corporate income tax if filed late; 20 percent if unpaid by statutory deadline; 0.022 percent daily interest accrues. Repeated non-filing may trigger enhanced penalty assessment and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Surtax Return on corporate income tax paid to central government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office (Si/Gun/Gu) via Local Tax System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the central corporate income tax return deadline; typically April 30 for calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional 10 percent of unpaid local surtax for late filing and 20 percent for non-payment by due date; daily penalty rate applies to unpaid amount. Persistent default may lead to property seizure or collection order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting resolution approving statutory financial statements and dividend distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders acting through the Chusik Hoesa corporate governance process; no public filing required for private unlisted companies except as provided by the Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, by January 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and auditors may be liable for losses resulting from a failure to convene the meeting; the NTS may deem unfiled financial statements as non-payment if the tax return remains absent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Amendment registration filings reflecting annual changes to directors, auditors, registered office, share capital, or shareholding structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office via the Korean Court Information Center (KICS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days from the date of the relevant corporate change; annual verification required at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposition of administrative fine (about USD 500 to 1,500) for late registration; continued non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off or dissolution by court order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment or Foreign Exchange Transaction report for non-resident shareholding changes and cross-border payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bank of Korea and relevant foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the underlying transaction or within 30 days after the annual AGM confirming shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties not exceeding KRW 100 million (about USD 74,000) for unreported transactions; criminal fines for intentional non-disclosure. Persistent breach may restrict outward remittances and require remedial registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent external audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million) as of the end of the prior fiscal year; mandatory audit also applies if the entity is listed, if 30 percent or more of shares are held by the State or local government, or if securing finance license or public benefit status requires audit. Enterprises below the threshold may have an optional review by a licensed accountant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean IFRS (K-IFRS) is mandatory for listed entities and strongly recommended for unlisted stock corporations; non-listed small and medium entities may apply Korean GAAP as approved by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At the annual general meeting, the directors must confirm the shareholders of record and the ultimate beneficial owners, particularly where any shareholding transfer occurred during the year. All transfers must be recorded in the register of members and, if a foreign investor becomes a major shareholder, a report must be made under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act within 30 days. The company must retain written records evidencing the identity of each beneficial owner for seven years; material changes to UBO details require amendment filing with the court registry within the same statutory filing window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Pledges and Warrants

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 to USD 3,500 per annum depending on district, office rent, and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 to USD 15,000 per annum for an independent certified audit under Korean IFRS or Korean GAAP, depending on revenue, asset base, and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (top national corporate income tax bracket applicable to taxable income above KRW 300 billion) plus a 10% local income tax surtax, producing a combined top headline effective rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory graduated national rates of 9%, 19%, and 21% for lower income bands; preferential deduction for foreign-invested enterprises under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act in Foreign Investment Zones (e.g., 100% relief for 5 years and 50% for the following 2 years); additional special tax credits for R&D expenditure (up to 25%-50% of qualifying R&D) and job creation under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; no industry-specific holiday for the aircraft parts distribution trade

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return Form 'Report on Tax Base and Tax Amount for Corporate Tax' (designated NTS form series, e.g., Form 40-1/40-2) filed exclusively through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr); large taxpayers use the same portal with mandatory e-filing of mandatory attachments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a mid-year interim corporate tax return for the first six-month period is additionally due for corporations whose tax amount in the immediately preceding fiscal year exceeded a statutory threshold
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (for a 31 December fiscal year end, by 31 March of the following year); if the corporate tax return is prepared and signed by a certified tax accountant (CPA or licensed tax attorney), the statutory deadline is automatically extended by 15 days

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross receipts from the trading of surplus commercial aircraft rotables and avionics, including export sales and freight-reimbursable amounts recognized under accrual accounting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation without a permanent establishment reports only Korea-source revenue; attach Form 40 and supporting schedule showing exclusion of foreign-source sales generated outside Korea

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Acquisition costs of surplus aircraft parts, import duties, inbound freight, insurance, hangar/logistics storage costs, and valuation adjustments recognized under the inventory valuation method
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportionment required for inbound parts destined to offshore buyers; only goods physically passing through Korea with title transfer in Korea are fully included

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 1 minus Box 2; the ABA gross margin on aviation spares trading must be benchmarked with arm's length comparables when related-party transactions are present
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents prepare a supplementary computation reconciling foreign branch/PE gross profit when the PE in Korea is the contracting party

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: airworthiness certification fees, inspection expenses, commissions to brokers, freight allowances, rent, salaries, insurance, and bank charges on escrow payment rails
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses incurred outside Korea that are directly allocable to Korea-source revenue may be deducted; apportionment statement must be attached

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of statutory non-deductible items under the Corporate Tax Act: entertainment expenses exceeding the threshold, unpaid income taxes, fines, interest penalties, bribes, and expenditures without proper documentation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE operations must add back head-office charges not satisfying arm's length conditions and without full service contracts

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income plus non-deductible add-backs, minus deductible reserves (e.g., warranty reserves, allowance for bad debts) and deductions for prior tax losses; output the statutory taxable income to which the progressive rate schedule is applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers compute Korea-source taxable income only and include gross-up adjustments for any withholding tax borne as final tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of graduated national rates 9%/19%/21%/24% to the taxable income bands, then the 10% local income tax surcharge on the calculated national tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation is assessed on a final-withholding basis; no surcharge item imposed where the income is already subject to statutory WHT unless the PE exists

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source receipts, R&D / job-creation credits, and credits for supporting investments; credits limited to the tax amount on the corresponding income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may use treaty credits only on income that is taxed again in Korea; attach the relevant DTA article and foreign TRC

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax from Box 7 minus credits in Box 8, after interim tax prepayment deductions; the amount actually paid with the annual return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any withholding tax already levied on the same income stream is credited against net tax, with refund claim protocol attached where treaty relief was not applied

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory schedules: balance sheet, income statement, statement of cash flows, related-party transactions report, international transaction disclosure form (Form 111), and transfer pricing documentation summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE filers attach the certificate of business registration in Korea, power of attorney of the local fiscal representative, and all WHT certificates

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file: penalty tax equal to 20% of the underpaid or unpaid corporate tax for an unfaithful or non-filed return; a false return under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act attracts criminal sanctions; underpayment itself triggers a daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022% per day on the deficient amount, approximating 8.03% on an annualized basis; failure to attach required related-party documents attracts an additional penalty and can void audit credit

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% combined at source for non-resident shareholders: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax (10% surcharge on the 20% national tax); DTA relief typically reduces the dividend withholding rate to 10%-15% depending on ownership, beneficial ownership, and the specific treaty provision
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must submit a written 'Application for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction' together with a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax competent authority, in advance or by the time of the distribution; the payer remits at treaty rate only while keeping the documentation on file; if the full statutory 22% was withheld, the non-resident must file a refund application through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal within the applicable statutory period (generally 3 years), attaching an apostilled or notarized TRC, proof of beneficial ownership (shareholding certificates, substance indicators), financial statements of the distributing company, and a power of attorney for any local tax representative
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 22% combined rate (20% national plus 2% local); treaty rate frequently 10% for portfolio bank interest and 15% for other interest subject to beneficial ownership test. Royalties for intellectual property (including avionics software licenses and certification data IP): statutory 22% combined; Korean DTAs typically reduce the rate to 10%-15%; treaty relief is denied if the recipient is a shell or lacks economic substance, and the beneficial ownership condition must be satisfied

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when the aggregate amount of international related-party transactions in a fiscal year exceeds KRW 5 billion; Master File is mandatory when annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion; separate reporting of related-party transactions is required on Form 111 when transactions with overseas related parties exceed KRW 100 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies the substance-over-form principle under the Framework Act on National Taxes and has fully integrated the OECD/G20 BEPS standard into the Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, including beneficial ownership analysis, Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clauses in current DTAs, and permanent establishment anti-abuse rules; although Korea has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation in the mould of the UAE ESR, a Chusik Hoesa that functions as a pure conduit or letterbox with no payroll, no physical offices, no genuine risk-taking, and no substantive inventory operations will be disregarded and denied treaty benefits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Fabricated Aviation Spares Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Preparing two sets of books, issuing inflated commercial invoices for surplus aircraft parts, understating export sales to offshore affiliates in low-tax jurisdictions (e.g., Hong Kong or Singapore), and supporting false deduction claims with fictitious repair and certification expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal punishment under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act: imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of not less than the amount evaded and up to 3 times the evaded tax; additional civil penalty of 20% of understated tax and a daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022%; tax authority may also conduct a criminal referral to the prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct fraudulent returns face criminal liability and are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax when corporate assets are insufficient; travel bans and departure prohibitions are issued during the audit, and the court may order forfeiture of proceeds derived from the evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Chusik Hoesa with no local employees, no inventory custody, no operating leases, no commercial substance, and no actual management meetings in Korea, used purely as a paper conduit for routing aircraft part sales to obtain treaty benefits or avoid recognition of a Korean PE
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service disregards the shell under the substance-over-form doctrine and the anti-avoidance provisions of the Framework Act; all revenue is recharacterized as taxable to the actual beneficial owner with disallowance of treaty withholding reduction (22% WHT re-imposed), additional TP adjustments, and other local corporate tax assessments plus daily surcharges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable under secondary tax liability rules for unpaid assessments after corporate assets are exhausted; travel bans and civil restitution orders are imposed; in aggravated cases involving cross-border aviation spare payments, the Act on Aggravated Punishment may extend imprisonment to directors who created the sham entity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering Violations on Escrowed Aviation Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring sales proceeds received via Escrow_Aviation and Swift Wire to conceal true payment for aircraft parts, using layered transfers through high-risk jurisdictions without Customer Due Diligence, conducting shell-to-shell invoice chaining, and failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports under the Financial Transactions Report Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine for the money-laundering offense under the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment; failure to file a suspicious transaction report is separately penalized by a fine; funds involved are subject to seizure and confiscation, and the entity may be blacklisted by financial institutions and denied banking access in Korea
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director in control of the payment processing is criminally liable alongside the corporation; personal assets are subject to confiscation, departure is prohibited through the issuance of an emigration restriction directive, and the court may impose imprisonment in excess of 5 years if the laundered amount exceeds KRW 500 million

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failures and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling surplus aircraft rotables to a related Hong Kong trader at artificially low margins so that profit accumulates in a zero-tax shell, while deliberately failing to prepare a Local File, Master File, or related-party transaction report within the statutorily mandated deadlines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may re-determine the taxable income based on the arm's length principle, impose additional corporate income tax and local income tax, and apply an unfaithful-return penalty of up to 20% plus daily interest surcharges; where records are wholly absent, the NTS may apply a deemed estimation and impose a further penalty under the Framework Act for non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the TP documentation or signed the tax return are jointly and severally liable for the deficiency if the corporation becomes insolvent; a director who intentionally omitted international transaction disclosures may face personal criminal prosecution for false reporting, and a travel restriction will be simultaneously imposed by the Minister of Justice, together with an order for civil restitution of the unpaid tax plus interest
